meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so you have twenty minutes. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first; start there.
You're clearly a brilliant lawyer, and I really respect how hard you fight for Owen.
Don't manage me, Hale. Who decided to enter that zero before anyone called me?
Can you step out of the role and tell me how I should handle this?
You're asking me how to do your job? We're not stepping anywhere, Hale. Withdraw the zero, or tell me what else you have.
I just want us to be on the same team here.
Then why are we here? You still haven't told me who entered that zero, or when.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require that Owen's zero be withdrawn, that I receive an apology for the mark being entered before anyone contacted me, and that nothing about this goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, with nothing agreed and the zero still under challenge.
What moved her: nothing, because no dated document tied to Owen's own work was put in front of her.
What cost ground: "tell me how I should handle this" cost the most, because asking her how to do your job lowered her respect for you; the flattery and the same-team appeal also bought nothing.
Try next time: when she asked who decided on the zero before anyone called her, say in one sentence that entering it first was wrong, then show her a dated document she can read herself.
